title: Who stole Max's bike?
scene: Max's bike disappears from the street. A cop and a detective look at the camera and see a silhouette; the main suspect, known for shoplifting and vandalism, has an alibi and a pretext, but the police find ganja in his pocket, check his dossier and give him a polygraph test - the vandal confesses.

old_story: One morning, Max's bike was gone from the street outside his building. He called the [[cops|cop]], and a young [[detective]] named Koval came an hour later. On the street camera, they saw the [[silhouette]] of a tall man at night. Koval knew him: a local guy with a history of [[shoplifting]] and [[vandalism]]. He had an [[alibi]]: he said he was at his aunt's house all night. The next day, he came back on the [[pretext]] of walking his dog. The police stopped him and found [[ganja]] in his pocket. Koval checked his [[dossier]] and asked for a [[polygraph]] test. Before the test even started, the young [[vandal]] confessed. He and an old soccer [[hooligan]] friend took the bike as a stupid joke. Max got his bike back that evening, with a scratch and a new lock.

old_story: On Friday night, Max watched an old film about the [[mafia]] with his dad. In it, an old [[gangster]] flies to Tokyo to meet the [[yakuza]]. The two groups start a long [[vendetta]] over drug [[trafficking]]. They fight about [[cannabis]] fields and boxes of [[opium]]. Behind them all is a huge crime [[syndicate]]. In the end, a police [[raid]] stops everything in one night. The police find [[bongs|bong]], a [[pistol]], and an old [[shotgun]] in the basement. An expert checks the [[caliber]] of every bullet. Max's dad fell asleep before the end, so Max had to tell him everything.

old_story: Anna listens to a true-crime podcast on her way to class. This week, the host talks about a [[maniac]] from an old case. A doctor explains that he was a [[psychopath]], not just a [[sadist]]. He was also a cruel [[abuser]], and his family lived with years of [[abuse]]. Later, he began [[stalking]] young women in his town. The police finally stopped him after a failed [[kidnapping]] with [[chloroform]]. In the second part, an expert explains how to protect children from a [[pedophile]] online. She also explains why [[incest]] and other family crimes often stay hidden. Then a [[coroner]] describes her work in the city [[morgue]]. She laughs and says her hobby is [[cannibalism]] in spiders. Anna takes off her headphones and decides to listen to music tonight.

title: Max builds a computer
scene: Max builds his own computer from new hardware. He reads the manual, puts every component and the processor into the right slot, adds memory as an upgrade, and tests the input, output and buffer; a friend shows him a high-tech prototype with old transistors, made by a famous innovator, that counts every byte.

old_story: Max decided to build his own [[desktop]] instead of buying one. He bought new [[hardware]] and spread it all over the kitchen table. First, he read the [[manual]] carefully, page by page. He checked every [[component]] and placed the [[processor]] very gently. He pushed extra memory into each [[slot]], a big [[upgrade]] for games. Then he tested the keyboard [[input]] and the screen [[output]] with a small program. A tiny [[buffer]] error appeared, but he fixed it in five minutes. That evening, his friend Ira brought an old [[prototype]] from her grandfather's garage. Its [[transistors|transistor]] were huge, and it could hold only one [[byte]] at a time. Max laughed: his new computer was a million times faster.

title: Max learns coding
scene: A programmer at Max's company teaches him coding. Max writes a test case, a tester reads the log, and the team builds an open source bot that answers every prompt; a contributor adds a plug-in that uses a weather API, and the beta goes to testers next week.

old_story: At Max's company, a [[programmer]] named Lena offered to teach him [[coding]]. On his first day, Max wrote a simple [[test case]] for the login page. A [[tester]] ran it and then read the [[log]] with him. Next, the team started a small [[open source]] project: a friendly help [[bot]]. The bot answers any [[prompt]] about the city's buses. Soon a [[contributor]] from Lviv added a [[plug-in]] for the weather. It uses a free weather [[API]], so the bot knows when it rains. Max asked the bot, "Do I need an umbrella?" It said yes. Next week, the [[beta]] goes to real users, and Max is a little nervous.
